_about: How a player earns each companion but Aki. The server decides from what it already knows and keeps the unlock for good; clients only show the condition and the progress `GET /api/unlocks/{user}` answers. `kind` is what counts: `level` (the player's level), `study_hours` (whole hours studied in total), `streak` (days in a row), `taps` (a chibi: an Easter egg found by tapping the picture of the companion `requires` names, its base, wherever the client shows the base; `goal` equals `taps`), `leeches_tamed` (cards with at least 8 lapses that later reached a 21-day interval, each card counted once). `goal` is the value that unlocks. A `secret` companion stays hidden until earned; the others show as a locked card with their condition. `status` is `live` when the companion can be earned, `planned` while it has no art yet: servers and clients ignore planned ones. Each check is a measured value of the companion's `kind` and whether it unlocks; the server (src/companions.rs) tests against them, planned companions included. Every `taps` entry names its base in `requires`, and a chibi stays locked until its base is unlocked: clients count taps only on a base that is unlocked and has a chibi, and the server refuses the chibi with 409 until the base is unlocked. The client counts the taps; on the run's last tap the chibi appears and the client sends `POST /api/unlocks/{user}` `{"unlock": "<chibi>"}` with no proof, which the server grants when the base is unlocked. The tap rule: `taps` taps on the base in a row, each not earlier than the one before and at most `max_gap_ms` after it (a tap at the same time continues the run); a tap on another choice, a longer gap, or a time before the one before starts the count again (that tap counts as the first of a new run). Times are 64-bit signed milliseconds; compute the gap without overflow. Each case lists the taps as [choice, milliseconds] and whether the last one unlocks; the base is unlocked in `cases`. From the `hint_from`th tap of a run until the one before the last, the client shows `hint` with {0} the taps still needed (`one` for 1, `other` otherwise); the last tap shows no hint, the chibi appears instead. `hints` gives the text after each tap count. Each `chibi_taps` case lists the unlocked companions, the taps, the hint after each tap (null for none) and whether the last tap unlocks. Each `requests` case is a `POST /api/unlocks/{user}` for the chibi from a player with `unlocked`, and the answer's `status`; `taps`, sent by apps released before this rule, is ignored.
